# Workstation's grid column drag proxy paints the theme's default colors

## Context

Found in manual testing of `apps/workstation` on `dev` (2026-10-22), in the same pass as #19982 and #19984. Dragging a column header of the 100k Matrix grid (here Throughput) shows a drag proxy whose header and cells use the neo theme's default grid colors: a blue header and near-black cells. Workstation's own palette is gone. A screenshot follows in a comment.

## Measurements

Headless Chromium, 1440×900, at `8bb3574d0f` (its `src/`, `apps/` and `resources/scss/` are identical to `dev` at `84b711878a`). A real pointer drag on the Throughput header, with computed styles read while the proxy is live:

| skin | property | source grid | drag proxy |
|---|---|---|---|
| dark | header background / text | `rgb(26,33,44)` / `rgb(214,220,230)` | `#182449` / `rgb(240,242,240)` |
| dark | cell background | `rgb(20,26,35)` | `#0E0F0D` |
| light | header background / text | `rgb(247,249,252)` / `rgb(31,39,51)` | `#5d83a7` / `#fff` |
| light | cell background | `#fff` | `#fff` |

The proxy is a direct child of `document.body` with `neo-grid-container neo-theme-neo-{dark,light} neo-dragproxy`. Its theme class is the live one in both skins. What is missing is Workstation's own skin.

## The Problem

Workstation skins grids with an app-scoped token bridge, not with a theme. `Viewport.scss` maps `--grid-*` onto its `--workstation-*` palette under `:root .workstation-viewport[class*="neo-theme-"], :root .workstation-viewport [class*="neo-theme-"]`, and sets the header tokens under `.workstation-viewport .neo-grid-header-button`.

The column-drag proxy is mounted outside that subtree. No bridge rule matches it, so every grid token on it resolves to the theme's default.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/draggable/DragZone.mjs`: `proxyParentId_` defaults to `'document.body'`, and the source's theme class is pushed onto the proxy.
- `src/draggable/grid/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs` `createDragProxy()`: `cls = ['neo-grid-container', owner.getTheme()]`. Inside, the proxy nests a `neo-grid-container` carrying the source grid's own `cls`, a header toolbar and cloned rows and cells.
- `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss`: the viewport bridge. Its comment explains why the selector mirrors the theme's own reach. For an inherited custom property the nearest declaring ancestor wins, and inner grid primitives carry skin classes too (#17984).
- **Design authority:** Workstation's own precedent for a body-mounted embodiment, the overflow menu in `Workspace.scss`. *"The generic menu is a second floating direct-body embodiment. Its own live `neo-theme-*` class carries the active palette; this Workstation-only bridge projects that palette into menu-domain tokens without coupling the shared tab plugin or shared menu component to product colours."* It is implemented as `body:has(.workstation-viewport) .neo-menu-list.neo-tab-overflow-menu { --menu-list-*: var(--workstation-*) }`. The grid proxy is a third such embodiment and has no bridge.

## The Fix

The fix is on the app side, in Workstation's SCSS; no engine change. The proxy already carries the live theme class and a grid identity.

1. Move the grid half of the viewport bridge into a single shared mixin, so the viewport scope and the proxy scope cannot drift. That half is the `--grid-container-*` and `--grid-cell-*` tokens, plus the `.neo-grid-header-button` token set, its justify-content and padding, and the glyph positioning.
2. Apply it to `body:has(.workstation-viewport) .neo-grid-container.neo-dragproxy`, **and** to every skin-carrying element inside the proxy (`… .neo-dragproxy [class*="neo-theme-"]`, mirroring the viewport bridge's shape). The proxy's inner `neo-grid-container` may carry its own theme class, and a bridge on the outer node alone would be shadowed there.

3. Put it in `Viewport.scss`, the sheet every boot mode loads. A `?popout=` vessel never loads `Workspace.css`, and a popped-out grid drags its columns too.

Specificity: `body:has(.workstation-viewport) .neo-grid-container.neo-dragproxy` is (0,3,1), against the theme's (0,2,0).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] While a 100k Matrix column header is being dragged, the proxy matches the source grid's computed values in both skins: header background, header text color, and each proxied cell's background against the source cell in the same row.
- [ ] The grid token bridge is declared once and shared by both scopes.
- [ ] **E2E:** a new spec under `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/` (e.g. `WorkstationGridDragProxySkinNL.spec.mjs`) starts a real pointer drag on a 100k Matrix column header and compares the live proxy's computed styles with the source's, in dark and then light (via the theme toggle). It must be red on `dev` (dark header `#182449` against `rgb(26,33,44)`) and green with the fix. It joins the hosted Workstation tier (#19655).
- [ ] Existing grid column-drag specs stay green.

## Out of Scope

- **A real Workstation theme.** None exists yet. A theme would give every body-mounted embodiment the right skin at once; this ticket keeps the current bridge model.
- **Other body-mounted embodiments** (tooltips, pickers, other menus). They were not reported and not audited here.

## Related

- #16120 (closed): a body-mounted dock tab drag proxy painted on a transparent surface. Same class, dock side.
- #17984 (closed): the viewport bridge's specificity contract.
- #19982, #19984: the same testing pass.
